title: Cogentrex — Memory, RAG, and Evaluation
purpose: Distinguish transient context, durable memory, retrieval, grounding, citations, and evaluation.
limitations: This is derivative learning material, not canonical implementation evidence.
SQL-JSON embeddings and Python cosine are not pgvector or an indexed vector service.
Deterministic checks and bounded live observations do not establish broad semantic quality or public deployment.

concepts.label: Effective Context
concepts.summary: Context is a bounded projection assembled for one provider call, not durable model memory.

teaching.definition: Effective context is the ordered, temporary request built from instructions, tool descriptions, selected facts, recent conversation rows, retrieval, images, and the current turn.
receives: Scoped facts, recent history, retrieval, and current input
teaching.responsibility: Select, order, compact, and bound provider-visible material while preserving scope and provenance metadata.
teaching.failure_behavior: Oversized provider-visible input fails before dispatch; lossy compaction remains explicit rather than pretending all stored history fit.
teaching.why_it_matters: A model can use only what was selected into this call, so context construction is a first-class reliability boundary.

concepts.boundary: Persisted provenance describes initial effective context, not every later model/tool iteration.
concepts.narration: Context is a packing list for one model call. Cogentrex selects instructions, tools, facts, recent history, retrieval, and current input under conservative bounds; the resulting window is not durable memory.
concepts.scenario: A fact exists in the database but is absent from the current context manifest.
options: Conclude it was not selected for this call
concepts.scenario_explanation: Durable storage and per-call selection are separate facts.

concepts.label: Conversation History
concepts.summary: Conversation rows are durable redacted dialogue; they are not runs, facts, or the entire context window.

teaching.definition: A conversation is owner-scoped metadata plus ordered redacted user and assistant messages that can span many runtime attempts.
teaching.responsibility: Preserve human dialogue and support bounded retrieval without mixing runtime events into visible message history.
produces: A bounded history input for context assembly
controls: Message persistence remains separate from run status
teaching.failure_behavior: A runtime interruption may leave a stored user turn without a completed assistant turn; the Run Ledger explains execution state.
teaching.why_it_matters: Stored dialogue answers what was said, while the ledger answers what the system did.

concepts.boundary: Deletion does not prove provider erasure, backup purge, or cryptographic erasure.
concepts.narration: Conversation history is durable redacted dialogue. One conversation can contain many runs, and only a bounded subset of its rows may enter a later model call.
concepts.scenario: A stored conversation has forty messages, but the request builder retrieves at most twenty.
options: Claim all forty reached the model
Explain that stored history exceeds selected context
Treat twenty as an exact token count
concepts.scenario_explanation: The retrieval bound is a selection rule, not storage loss or a token guarantee.

concepts.label: Encrypted Fact Memory
concepts.summary: Selected owner/project facts are redacted, AES-GCM encrypted, authenticated, quota-bounded, and explicitly projected into context.

teaching.definition: Encrypted memory is a durable fact store whose ciphertext is bound to owner, project, fact identity, and key version through derived keys and authenticated associated data.
teaching.responsibility: Redact, encrypt, authenticate, quota-check, persist, and selectively decrypt facts for authorized use.
teaching.failure_behavior: Wrong keys, tampering, malformed envelopes, or row substitution fail closed; key loss makes facts unreadable.
teaching.why_it_matters: Durable personalization needs confidentiality, integrity, scope, and explicit selection rather than an anthropomorphic memory claim.

concepts.boundary: Selected plaintext exists in process and provider input; external KMS and automatic expiry are not claimed.
concepts.narration: Fact memory is separate from conversation history. Cogentrex redacts and encrypts selected facts with scope-bound authenticated encryption, then decrypts only for an authorized projection into context.
concepts.scenario: Two ciphertext rows under one project are swapped between fact IDs.
options: Fail authentication because AAD binds the fact ID
Send them to the provider for validation
concepts.scenario_explanation: Authenticated associated data prevents silent row substitution.

concepts.label: Chunking
concepts.summary: Recursive character-aware splitting creates bounded retrieval units with overlap and integrity metadata.

teaching.definition: Chunking divides document text into indexed units by preferring paragraph, newline, sentence, word, then hard character boundaries.
teaching.responsibility: Create inspectable retrieval units while reducing boundary loss through measured overlap.
teaching.failure_behavior: Separator-free or poorly extracted text can split meaning; excessive overlap can crowd retrieval with duplicates.
teaching.why_it_matters: Retrieval can return only the units the ingestion path created, so boundaries directly affect evidence availability.

concepts.boundary: Character counts are not tokenizer-aware limits, and default size/overlap are not universally optimal.
concepts.narration: Chunking defines what retrieval can return. Cogentrex uses inspectable recursive character boundaries and overlap, but those defaults need corpus-specific evaluation rather than folklore.
concepts.scenario: Increasing overlap raises duplicate top-k results without improving labeled recall.
options: Reduce overlap based on measured recall and redundancy
concepts.scenario_explanation: Overlap is a trade-off and must be evaluated downstream.

concepts.label: Embeddings
concepts.summary: Validated vectors provide a similarity space; geometry is a ranking signal, not truth or authorization.

teaching.definition: An embedding maps text into a fixed-dimensional numeric vector whose direction can be compared with a query vector.
teaching.responsibility: Produce finite vectors in one compatible space and reject malformed, mismatched, or unsafe provider responses.
teaching.failure_behavior: Wrong counts, indexes, dimensions, non-finite values, or unsafe endpoints fail closed rather than entering the index.
teaching.why_it_matters: Similarity calculations are meaningful only when vectors share a validated model and configuration.

concepts.boundary: One Foundry sentinel proves bounded development behavior, not domain recall, production SLA, or semantic truth.
concepts.narration: Embeddings place questions and chunks in one numeric space. Cogentrex validates vectors and provider boundaries, but similarity remains a retrieval signal rather than proof that a source or answer is true.
concepts.scenario: A mock hash embedding ranks an unrelated chunk first.
options: Treat it as deterministic plumbing only
concepts.scenario_explanation: Determinism does not create semantic geometry.

concepts.label: Scoped Retrieval
concepts.summary: Owner/project SQL predicates narrow rows before Python cosine ranks a bounded candidate set.

teaching.definition: Retrieval selects candidate chunks that may help answer a question, after legal scope is applied and persisted integrity is checked.
teaching.responsibility: Load a bounded authorized candidate set, skip corrupt rows, compute cosine in Python, deduplicate evidence, and return top-k results.
teaching.failure_behavior: Corrupt rows are skipped safely; an explicitly empty document set returns no results; bounded scans can miss relevant rows.
teaching.why_it_matters: Searching broadly and filtering afterward would leak data and distort ranking across tenants.

concepts.boundary: The backend is sql-json-cosine, not pgvector, ANN, or a high-scale indexed service.
concepts.narration: Retrieval applies owner and project filters in SQL before ranking. Valid JSON vectors are scored with Python cosine, making the current backend inspectable but deliberately not pgvector.
concepts.scenario: A design loads every tenant's chunks, computes scores, then removes foreign rows.
options: Reject because scope must precede loading and ranking
concepts.scenario_explanation: Authorization must constrain the candidate set before data is loaded.

concepts.label: Grounded Generation
concepts.summary: The grounded workflow requests bounded atomic claims from retrieved evidence and abstains when evidence is absent.

teaching.definition: Grounded generation is a structured synthesis step that asks the provider for atomic claims linked to known run-local evidence IDs.
teaching.responsibility: Request one-call structured claims without granting retrieved text authority over tools or policy.
controls: No-evidence path makes zero provider calls
Output, claim, and citation counts are bounded
teaching.failure_behavior: No evidence yields abstention; malformed output, provider errors, or cancellation produce explicit safe terminal behavior.
teaching.why_it_matters: Putting text in a prompt does not guarantee the model will use it correctly, so generation remains untrusted input to verification.

concepts.boundary: Prompt instructions such as use-only-evidence are controls, not proof of faithfulness.
concepts.narration: The grounded path asks for atomic claims and known evidence IDs. If retrieval finds nothing, it abstains without calling the model; if generation succeeds, verification still decides what survives.
concepts.scenario: Retrieval returns no evidence for the question.
options: Return the standard abstention with zero provider calls
Use the highest score from another project
concepts.scenario_explanation: No evidence is an explicit abstention path.

concepts.label: Claim Verification
concepts.summary: Hash, citation, token, number, and polarity checks conservatively filter unsupported claims.

teaching.definition: Claim verification compares each generated atomic claim with its cited evidence under repeatable integrity and support rules.
teaching.responsibility: Reject unknown citations, changed evidence, weak token support, changed numbers, and polarity mismatches before answer reconstruction.
controls: Failure is not rewritten as support
teaching.failure_behavior: Missing, unknown, malformed, tampered, or insufficient support fails closed; lexical checks may reject valid paraphrases or accept word-overlap impostors.
teaching.why_it_matters: A provider's confidence cannot substitute for an inspectable support decision.

concepts.boundary: Deterministic lexical, numeric, and polarity checks are not semantic entailment or global fact checking.
concepts.narration: Verification rechecks evidence identity, citations, numbers, polarity, and substantive overlap. It is conservative, repeatable defense in depth—not semantic truth or an oracle.
concepts.scenario: A claim changes a cited value from twenty to two hundred while keeping most words.
options: Reject because claim numbers must occur in evidence
Ask retrieval for a confidence score
concepts.scenario_explanation: Numeric containment catches this specific overclaim.

concepts.label: Citations
concepts.summary: A citation binds one claim to run-local evidence identity, integrity metadata, and a bounded inspectable quote.

teaching.definition: A citation is a claim-specific receipt linking a visible E-number to document ID, chunk ID, content hash, and bounded evidence metadata.
teaching.responsibility: Preserve the claim-to-evidence relationship and expose only citations actually used by supported claims.
teaching.failure_behavior: A valid marker attached to irrelevant evidence remains citation-incorrect; broken provenance must fail visibly rather than resolve to replacement text.
teaching.why_it_matters: Decorative brackets create false confidence unless the exact source relationship can be inspected.

concepts.boundary: A correct citation can point to a false or stale source and can accompany an answer that is irrelevant.
concepts.narration: Citations are claim-specific receipts. An E-number matters only inside its run and must resolve through document, chunk, and content hash to evidence that actually supports the claim.
concepts.scenario: Every claim has an E marker, but one marker points to unrelated text.
options: Delete unsupported claims from the ledger
Treat E numbers as global IDs
concepts.scenario_explanation: Structural coverage does not establish support correctness.

concepts.label: Recorded-run Evaluation
concepts.summary: Versioned fixtures measure completed persisted trajectories without rerunning the model, retriever, or tools.

teaching.definition: Recorded-run evaluation is a post-run service that maps versioned case keys to completed scoped runs and persists deterministic checks, metrics, and aggregates.
receives: All safe events from completed runs
teaching.responsibility: Reconstruct repeatable measurements without fabricating alternate answers or mutating source runs.
teaching.failure_behavior: Changed fixtures, duplicate mappings, active runs, missing events, or partial persistence fail validation or finalize as failed.
teaching.why_it_matters: Evaluation can reproduce a measurement only when dataset identity, source-run identity, and calculation are all inspectable.

concepts.boundary: A precise deterministic ruler may measure the wrong property; current fixtures do not prove broad live-model quality or learning.
concepts.narration: Evaluation happens after execution. Versioned, hash-checked fixtures map to completed run IDs and produce durable metrics without calling runtime dependencies. Reproducibility still does not guarantee metric validity.
concepts.scenario: A two-case deterministic fixture passes on scripted trajectories.
options: Report regression evidence within the fixture boundary
concepts.scenario_explanation: The evidence is useful but narrow and must retain its scope.
